state.question: Why do all four independent measurement streams show significant negative autocorrelations at lags of 7–8 days, and why do cross-instrument correlations cluster around moderate negative or weak positive values with consistent 5–6 day offsets, when instruments measuring the same physical constants should either track together tightly or drift independently?

hypotheses.label: Systematic environmental cyclic forcing with ~7-day period
hypotheses.rationale: The autocorrelation pattern (pendulum_lab: -0.600 at lag 8; pendulum_obs: -0.446 at lag 7; resonator_lab: 0.400 at lag 8; resonator_obs: -0.348 at lag 7) is too coherent across instruments to be noise. A 7–8 day environmental cycle (temperature, humidity, barometric pressure, or structural vibration) could induce readings to swing negative relative to their values one week prior—a classic signature of aliased periodic forcing. The cross-instrument 5–6 day offsets suggest coupling through a shared environmental medium rather than independent instrumental error. Resonator_lab's positive autocorr at lag 8 (vs. negative elsewhere) is consistent with a nonlinear or phase-dependent response to the same cycle.

hypotheses.label: Instrumental calibration drift with 7-day re-zeroing or reset cycle
hypotheses.rationale: The negative autocorrelations at lag 7–8 could reflect a systematic procedural artifact: if instruments are recalibrated, zeroed, or inspected on a weekly schedule (e.g., end of Day 7), a reading on Day 1 would be expected to anti-correlate with the reading on Day 8 (post-reset). Each stream shows this pattern independently, suggesting all four instruments are on the same maintenance schedule. Cross-instrument offsets (5–6 days) would then reflect staggered calibration or partial re-zeroing events.
